passages.text: Now the famine was still severe in the land.
passages.sermon: A famine struck the land.\r\nThe famine was very severe.\r\nThe people in the land suffered greatly.
passages.original: וְהָרָעָ֖ב כָּבֵ֥ד בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: So when Jacob’s sons had eaten all the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, “Go back and buy us a little more food.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the father of these sons.
A severe famine was in the land.
Jacob’s sons brought grain from Egypt.
They finished eating all the grain.
Jacob spoke to his sons.
He said, “Go back.”
He said, “Buy us a little more food.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר כִּלּוּ֙ לֶאֱכֹ֣ל אֶת־ הַשֶּׁ֔בֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵבִ֖יאוּ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ אֲבִיהֶ֔ם שֻׁ֖בוּ שִׁבְרוּ־ לָ֥נוּ מְעַט־ אֹֽכֶל׃

passages.text: But Judah replied, “The man solemnly warned us, ‘You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.’
passages.sermon:
Judah spoke to his father.
Judah said, "The man warned us strongly."
The man said, 'You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.'
The man in Egypt gave this warning.
The man meant we cannot return without our brother.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלָ֛יו יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר הָעֵ֣ד הֵעִד֩ בָּ֨נוּ הָאִ֤ישׁ לֵאמֹר֙ לֹֽא־ תִרְא֣וּ פָנַ֔י בִּלְתִּ֖י אֲחִיכֶ֥ם אִתְּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.
passages.sermon: Judah spoke to his father Jacob.\r\nJudah said, “If you send our brother Benjamin with us, we will go to Egypt.\r\nWe will buy food for you.”
passages.original: אִם־ יֶשְׁךָ֛ מְשַׁלֵּ֥חַ אֶת־ אָחִ֖ינוּ אִתָּ֑נוּ נֵרְדָ֕ה וְנִשְׁבְּרָ֥ה לְךָ֖ אֹֽכֶל׃

passages.text: But if you will not send him, we will not go; for the man told us, ‘You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Judah spoke to his father Israel.
Judah said, "If you do not send our brother with us, we will not go down to Egypt."
The man in Egypt warned us.
He said, 'You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.'
passages.original: וְאִם־ אֵינְךָ֥ מְשַׁלֵּ֖חַ לֹ֣א נֵרֵ֑ד כִּֽי־ הָאִ֞ישׁ אָמַ֤ר אֵלֵ֙ינוּ֙ לֹֽא־ תִרְא֣וּ פָנַ֔י בִּלְתִּ֖י אֲחִיכֶ֥ם אִתְּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: “Why did you bring this trouble upon me?” Israel asked. “Why did you tell the man you had another brother?”
passages.sermon:
Israel was the father of the brothers.
Israel spoke to his sons.
Israel asked, “Why did you bring this trouble to me?”
Israel said, “Why did you tell the man you have another brother?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָמָ֥ה הֲרֵעֹתֶ֖ם לִ֑י לְהַגִּ֣יד לָאִ֔ישׁ הַע֥וֹד לָכֶ֖ם אָֽח׃

passages.text: They replied, “The man questioned us in detail about ourselves and our family: ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?’ And we answered him accordingly. How could we possibly know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother here’?”
passages.sermon:
The brothers spoke to their father Israel.
They said, "The man questioned us closely.
He asked about us.
He asked about our family.
He said, 'Is your father still alive?'
He said, 'Do you have another brother?'
We answered him as he asked.
We told him what he wanted to know.
We did not know he would say, 'Bring your brother here.'
We could not have known he would ask for our brother to come."
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֡וּ שָׁא֣וֹל שָֽׁאַל־ הָ֠אִישׁ לָ֣נוּ וּלְמֽוֹלַדְתֵּ֜נוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר הַע֨וֹד אֲבִיכֶ֥ם חַי֙ הֲיֵ֣שׁ לָכֶ֣ם אָ֔ח וַנַ֨גֶּד־ ל֔וֹ עַל־ פִּ֖י הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה הֲיָד֣וֹעַ נֵדַ֔ע כִּ֣י יֹאמַ֔ר הוֹרִ֖ידוּ אֶת־ אֲחִיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: And Judah said to his father Israel, “Send the boy with me, and we will go at once, so that we may live and not die—neither we, nor you, nor our children.
passages.sermon:
Judah spoke to his father Israel.
Judah said, "Send the boy with me."
We will get up and go right away.
We will live and not die.
You will live.
We will live.
Our children will live.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוּדָ֜ה אֶל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אָבִ֗יו שִׁלְחָ֥ה הַנַּ֛עַר אִתִּ֖י וְנָק֣וּמָה וְנֵלֵ֑כָה וְנִֽחְיֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א נָמ֔וּת גַּם־ אֲנַ֥חְנוּ גַם־ אַתָּ֖ה גַּם־ טַפֵּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: I will guarantee his safety. You may hold me personally responsible. If I do not bring him back and set him before you, then may I bear the guilt before you all my life.
passages.sermon:
Judah spoke to his father Israel.
Judah promised to take care of Benjamin.
Judah said, "I will guarantee his safety."
Judah told his father, "You may hold me responsible."
Judah said, "If I do not bring Benjamin back to you, and set him before you, I will be guilty before you all my life."
passages.original: אָֽנֹכִי֙ אֶֽעֶרְבֶ֔נּוּ מִיָּדִ֖י תְּבַקְשֶׁ֑נּוּ אִם־ לֹ֨א הֲבִיאֹתִ֤יו אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ וְהִצַּגְתִּ֣יו לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְחָטָ֥אתִֽי לְךָ֖ כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: If we had not delayed, we could have come and gone twice by now.”
passages.sermon: Judah spoke to his father Israel.\r\nJudah said these words.\r\nIf we had not waited so long, we could have traveled there and back twice already.
passages.original: כִּ֖י לוּלֵ֣א הִתְמַהְמָ֑הְנוּ כִּֽי־ עַתָּ֥ה שַׁ֖בְנוּ זֶ֥ה פַעֲמָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Then their father Israel said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: Put some of the best products of the land in your packs and carry them down as a gift for the man—a little balm and a little honey, spices and myrrh, pistachios and almonds.
passages.sermon:
Israel was their father.
Israel spoke to his sons.
Israel said, “If it must be so, do this.
Take some of the best products of the land.
Put them in your packs.
Carry them down as a gift for the man.
Take a little balm.
Take a little honey.
Take some spices.
Take some myrrh.
Take pistachios.
Take almonds.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אֲבִיהֶ֗ם אִם־ כֵּ֣ן׀ אֵפוֹא֮ זֹ֣את עֲשׂוּ֒ קְח֞וּ מִזִּמְרַ֤ת הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ בִּכְלֵיכֶ֔ם וְהוֹרִ֥ידוּ לָאִ֖ישׁ מִנְחָ֑ה מְעַ֤ט צֳרִי֙ וּמְעַ֣ט דְּבַ֔שׁ נְכֹ֣את וָלֹ֔ט בָּטְנִ֖ים וּשְׁקֵדִֽים׃

passages.text: Take double the silver with you so that you may return the silver that was put back into the mouths of your sacks. Perhaps it was a mistake.
passages.sermon:
Israel was the father of the men.
Israel spoke to his sons.
He told them to take double the silver with them.
He told them to carry the silver in their hands.
He told them to return the silver that was put back into the mouths of their sacks.
He said, "Perhaps it was a mistake."
passages.original: וְכֶ֥סֶף מִשְׁנֶ֖ה קְח֣וּ בְיֶדְכֶ֑ם וְאֶת־ הַכֶּ֜סֶף הַמּוּשָׁ֨ב בְּפִ֤י אַמְתְּחֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ תָּשִׁ֣יבוּ בְיֶדְכֶ֔ם אוּלַ֥י מִשְׁגֶּ֖ה הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Take your brother as well, and return to the man at once.
passages.sermon:
Israel was their father.
Israel spoke to his sons.
He told them to take their brother with them.
He told them to get up.
He told them to return to the man immediately.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ אֲחִיכֶ֖ם קָ֑חוּ וְק֖וּמוּ שׁ֥וּבוּ אֶל־ הָאִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man, that he may release your other brother along with Benjamin. As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved.”
passages.sermon:
God Almighty is powerful and merciful.
God Almighty can show you mercy.
You will stand before the man in Egypt.
I pray God will give you favor with him.
I pray the man will release your other brother.
I pray the man will also release Benjamin.
If I lose my children, then I am bereaved.
passages.original: וְאֵ֣ל שַׁדַּ֗י יִתֵּ֨ן לָכֶ֤ם רַחֲמִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָאִ֔ישׁ וְשִׁלַּ֥ח לָכֶ֛ם אֶת־ אֲחִיכֶ֥ם אַחֵ֖ר וְאֶת־ בִּנְיָמִ֑ין וַאֲנִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁכֹ֖לְתִּי שָׁכָֽלְתִּי׃

passages.text: So the men took these gifts, along with double the amount of silver, and Benjamin as well. Then they hurried down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.
passages.sermon:
The men took the gifts.
They took double the amount of silver in their hands.
They took Benjamin with them.
They got up.
They went down to Egypt.
They stood before Joseph.
passages.original: וַיִּקְח֤וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֶת־ הַמִּנְחָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את וּמִשְׁנֶה־ כֶּ֛סֶף לָקְח֥וּ בְיָדָ֖ם וְאֶת־ בִּנְיָמִ֑ן וַיָּקֻ֙מוּ֙ וַיֵּרְד֣וּ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיַּֽעַמְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י יוֹסֵֽף׃

passages.text: When Joseph saw Benjamin with his brothers, he said to the steward of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and prepare it, for they shall dine with me at noon.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the governor of Egypt.
Joseph saw his brothers.
Joseph saw Benjamin with them.
Joseph spoke to the steward of his house.
Joseph said, "Bring these men to my house."
Joseph said, "Slaughter an animal and prepare it."
Joseph said, "These men will eat with me at noon."
passages.original: וַיַּ֨רְא יוֹסֵ֣ף אִתָּם֮ אֶת־ בִּנְיָמִין֒ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לַֽאֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ בֵּית֔וֹ הָבֵ֥א אֶת־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים הַבָּ֑יְתָה וּטְבֹ֤חַ טֶ֙בַח֙ וְהָכֵ֔ן כִּ֥י אִתִּ֛י יֹאכְל֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים בַּֽצָּהֳרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: The man did as Joseph had commanded and took the brothers to Joseph’s house.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the ruler in Egypt.
Joseph gave a command to his steward.
The steward was the man in charge of Joseph’s house.
The steward obeyed Joseph.
The steward took Joseph’s brothers.
The steward brought the brothers into Joseph’s house.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ הָאִ֔ישׁ כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֣ר יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיָּבֵ֥א הָאִ֛ישׁ אֶת־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים בֵּ֥יתָה יוֹסֵֽף׃

passages.text: But the brothers were frightened that they had been taken to Joseph’s house. “We have been brought here because of the silver that was returned in our bags the first time,” they said. “They intend to overpower us and take us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph’s brothers felt afraid.
They saw that someone brought them to Joseph’s house.
They said, “We have been brought here because of the silver.”
They remembered the silver that someone returned in their bags the first time.
They said, “They want to accuse us.”
“They want to attack us.”
“They want to take us as slaves.”
“They want to take our donkeys too.”
passages.original: וַיִּֽירְא֣וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֗ים כִּ֣י הֽוּבְאוּ֮ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵף֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ עַל־ דְּבַ֤ר הַכֶּ֙סֶף֙ הַשָּׁ֤ב בְּאַמְתְּחֹתֵ֙ינוּ֙ בַּתְּחִלָּ֔ה אֲנַ֖חְנוּ מֽוּבָאִ֑ים לְהִתְגֹּלֵ֤ל עָלֵ֙ינוּ֙ וּלְהִתְנַפֵּ֣ל עָלֵ֔ינוּ וְלָקַ֧חַת אֹתָ֛נוּ לַעֲבָדִ֖ים וְאֶת־ חֲמֹרֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: So they approached Joseph’s steward and spoke to him at the entrance to the house.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a powerful leader in Egypt.
Joseph had a steward who managed his house.
Joseph’s brothers were in Egypt.
The brothers felt afraid.
The brothers went to Joseph’s steward.
They met him at the entrance of Joseph’s house.
The brothers spoke to the steward.
passages.original: וַֽיִּגְּשׁוּ֙ אֶל־ הָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו פֶּ֥תַח הַבָּֽיִת׃

passages.text: “Please, sir,” they said, “we really did come down here the first time to buy food.
passages.sermon:
Joseph’s brothers spoke to Joseph’s steward.
They said, “Please, sir.
We came down to Egypt the first time.
We came to buy food.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֑י יָרֹ֥ד יָרַ֛דְנוּ בַּתְּחִלָּ֖ה לִשְׁבָּר־ אֹֽכֶל׃

passages.text: But when we came to the place we lodged for the night, we opened our sacks and, behold, each of us found his silver in the mouth of his sack! It was the full amount of our silver, and we have brought it back with us.
passages.sermon:
Joseph’s brothers traveled to Egypt to buy food.
They stopped for the night at a lodging place.
They opened their sacks.
Each brother found his own silver in the mouth of his sack.
The silver was the full amount they had brought.
They brought this silver back with them.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִ֞י כִּי־ בָ֣אנוּ אֶל־ הַמָּל֗וֹן וַֽנִּפְתְּחָה֙ אֶת־ אַמְתְּחֹתֵ֔ינוּ וְהִנֵּ֤ה כֶֽסֶף־ אִישׁ֙ בְּפִ֣י אַמְתַּחְתּ֔וֹ כַּסְפֵּ֖נוּ בְּמִשְׁקָל֑וֹ וַנָּ֥שֶׁב אֹת֖וֹ בְּיָדֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: We have brought additional silver with us to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our sacks.”
passages.sermon:
The brothers of Joseph spoke to the steward in Egypt.
They said, “We have brought more silver with us.
We want to buy food with this silver.
We do not know who put our silver in our sacks.”
passages.original: וְכֶ֧סֶף אַחֵ֛ר הוֹרַ֥דְנוּ בְיָדֵ֖נוּ לִשְׁבָּר־ אֹ֑כֶל לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְנוּ מִי־ שָׂ֥ם כַּסְפֵּ֖נוּ בְּאַמְתְּחֹתֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: “It is fine,” said the steward. “Do not be afraid. Your God, the God of your father, gave you the treasure that was in your sacks. I received your silver.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
passages.sermon:
The steward spoke to the brothers.
He said, "Peace to you."
He said, "Do not be afraid."
He said, "Your God gave you the treasure in your sacks."
He said, "The God of your father did this."
He said, "I received your silver."
Then the steward brought Simeon out to them.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ שָׁל֨וֹם לָכֶ֜ם אַל־ תִּירָ֗אוּ אֱלֹ֨הֵיכֶ֜ם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֤י אֲבִיכֶם֙ נָתַ֨ן לָכֶ֤ם מַטְמוֹן֙ בְּאַמְתְּחֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם כַּסְפְּכֶ֖ם בָּ֣א אֵלָ֑י וַיּוֹצֵ֥א אֲלֵהֶ֖ם אֶת־ שִׁמְעֽוֹן׃

passages.text: And the steward took the men into Joseph’s house, gave them water to wash their feet, and provided food for their donkeys.
passages.sermon:
The steward worked for Joseph.
The steward took the men into Joseph’s house.
The steward gave the men water.
The men washed their feet.
The steward gave food to their donkeys.
passages.original: וַיָּבֵ֥א הָאִ֛ישׁ אֶת־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים בֵּ֣יתָה יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיִּתֶּן־ מַ֙יִם֙ וַיִּרְחֲצ֣וּ רַגְלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּתֵּ֥ן מִסְפּ֖וֹא לַחֲמֹֽרֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Since the brothers had been told that they were going to eat a meal there, they prepared their gift for Joseph’s arrival at noon.
passages.sermon:
Joseph’s brothers waited in Egypt.
They had a gift for Joseph.
They prepared the gift.
They got ready before Joseph arrived at noon.
They knew they would eat a meal there.
They heard they would eat bread in Joseph’s house.
passages.original: וַיָּכִ֙ינוּ֙ אֶת־ הַמִּנְחָ֔ה עַד־ בּ֥וֹא יוֹסֵ֖ף בַּֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם כִּ֣י שָֽׁמְע֔וּ כִּי־ שָׁ֖ם יֹ֥אכְלוּ לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: When Joseph came home, they presented him with the gifts they had brought, and they bowed to the ground before him.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the ruler of Egypt.
Joseph came home.
The brothers had brought gifts for Joseph.
The brothers carried the gifts in their hands.
The brothers brought the gifts into Joseph’s house.
The brothers gave the gifts to Joseph.
The brothers bowed down to the ground before Joseph.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א יוֹסֵף֙ הַבַּ֔יְתָה וַיָּבִ֥יאּוּ ל֛וֹ אֶת־ הַמִּנְחָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־ בְּיָדָ֖ם הַבָּ֑יְתָה וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ־ ל֖וֹ אָֽרְצָה׃

passages.text: He asked if they were well, and then he asked, “How is your elderly father you told me about? Is he still alive?”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the ruler in Egypt.
Joseph’s brothers came to him.
Joseph asked his brothers if they were well.
Joseph said, “How is your elderly father?”
Joseph said, “He is the father you told me about.”
Joseph asked, “Is your father still alive?”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל לָהֶם֙ לְשָׁל֔וֹם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲשָׁל֛וֹם אֲבִיכֶ֥ם הַזָּקֵ֖ן אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲמַרְתֶּ֑ם הַעוֹדֶ֖נּוּ חָֽי׃

passages.text: “Your servant our father is well,” they answered. “He is still alive.” And they bowed down to honor him.
passages.sermon:
Joseph’s brothers spoke to him.
They answered Joseph’s question about their father.
They said, “Our father, your servant, is well.”
They said, “He is still alive.”
They bowed down before Joseph.
They honored him by bowing.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ שָׁל֛וֹם לְעַבְדְּךָ֥ לְאָבִ֖ינוּ עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ חָ֑י וַֽיִּקְּד֖וּ וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ׃

passages.text: When Joseph looked up and saw his brother Benjamin, his own mother’s son, he asked, “Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?” Then he declared, “May God be gracious to you, my son.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the governor of Egypt.
Joseph was a Hebrew.
Joseph had brothers who came to Egypt.
Joseph’s mother was Rachel.
Benjamin was Joseph’s only full brother.
Joseph looked up.
Joseph saw Benjamin.
Benjamin was his brother.
Benjamin was the son of Joseph’s mother.
Joseph asked a question.
Joseph said, “Is this your youngest brother?”
Joseph meant the brother they had told him about.
Joseph spoke to Benjamin.
Joseph said, “May God be gracious to you, my son.”
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֣א עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּ֞רְא אֶת־ בִּנְיָמִ֣ין אָחִיו֮ בֶּן־ אִמּוֹ֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲזֶה֙ אֲחִיכֶ֣ם הַקָּטֹ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֵלָ֑י וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים יָחְנְךָ֖ בְּנִֽי׃

passages.text: Joseph hurried out because he was moved to tears for his brother, and he went to a private room to weep.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the ruler in Egypt.
Joseph saw his brother Benjamin.
Joseph felt deep compassion for his brother.
Joseph wanted to cry.
Joseph quickly left the room.
Joseph went into a private room.
Joseph wept there.
passages.original: וַיְמַהֵ֣ר יוֹסֵ֗ף כִּֽי־ נִכְמְר֤וּ רַחֲמָיו֙ אֶל־ אָחִ֔יו וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לִבְכּ֑וֹת וַיָּבֹ֥א הַחַ֖דְרָה וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ שָֽׁמָּה׃

passages.text: Then he washed his face and came back out. Regaining his composure, he said, “Serve the meal.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the governor of Egypt.
Joseph was a Hebrew.
Joseph had just seen his brother Benjamin.
Joseph felt strong emotions and went to a private room to weep.
Joseph washed his face.
Joseph came out of the room.
Joseph controlled his feelings.
Joseph said, “Serve the meal.”
passages.original: וַיִּרְחַ֥ץ פָּנָ֖יו וַיֵּצֵ֑א וַיִּ֨תְאַפַּ֔ק וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שִׂ֥ימוּ לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: They separately served Joseph, his brothers, and the Egyptians. They ate separately because the Egyptians would not eat with the Hebrews, since that was detestable to them.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a Hebrew leader in Egypt.
Joseph’s brothers were Hebrews.
The Egyptians were the native people of Egypt.
The servants set a table for Joseph alone.
They set a separate table for Joseph’s brothers.
They set another table for the Egyptians who ate with Joseph.
The Egyptians would not eat bread with the Hebrews.
The Egyptians thought eating with Hebrews was detestable.
passages.original: וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ ל֛וֹ לְבַדּ֖וֹ וְלָהֶ֣ם לְבַדָּ֑ם וְלַמִּצְרִ֞ים הָאֹכְלִ֤ים אִתּוֹ֙ לְבַדָּ֔ם כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יוּכְל֜וּן הַמִּצְרִ֗ים לֶאֱכֹ֤ל אֶת־ הָֽעִבְרִים֙ לֶ֔חֶם כִּי־ תוֹעֵבָ֥ה הִ֖וא לְמִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: They were seated before Joseph in order by age, from the firstborn to the youngest, and the men looked at one another in astonishment.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the ruler in Egypt.
Joseph’s brothers came to eat with him.
Joseph’s servants seated the brothers in front of Joseph.
They placed the oldest brother first.
They placed each brother in order by age.
They placed the youngest brother last.
The brothers saw the order.
The brothers were surprised.
Each man looked at his neighbor in astonishment.
passages.original: וַיֵּשְׁב֣וּ לְפָנָ֔יו הַבְּכֹר֙ כִּבְכֹ֣רָת֔וֹ וְהַצָּעִ֖יר כִּצְעִרָת֑וֹ וַיִּתְמְה֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אִ֥ישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: When the portions were served to them from Joseph’s table, Benjamin’s portion was five times larger than any of the others. So they feasted and drank freely with Joseph.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the ruler of Egypt.
Joseph’s brothers came to eat with him.
Joseph gave food portions to his brothers.
Joseph gave Benjamin a much larger portion.
Benjamin’s portion was five times bigger than the others.
Joseph and his brothers ate together.
They drank together.
They became drunk with Joseph.
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א מַשְׂאֹ֜ת מֵאֵ֣ת פָּנָיו֮ אֲלֵהֶם֒ וַתֵּ֜רֶב מַשְׂאַ֧ת בִּנְיָמִ֛ן מִמַּשְׂאֹ֥ת כֻּלָּ֖ם חָמֵ֣שׁ יָד֑וֹת וַיִּשְׁתּ֥וּ וַֽיִּשְׁכְּר֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃
